mappings.name: webpayment: accepted, with a pay_token derived from the order_id

file: POST {base}/v1/webpayment — the submit call. Selection is by the
body's `order_id`, which is ChargeRef::reference_id rendered as a
string, so these are the same UUIDs the MTN mappings match on
`X-Reference-Id`. See the mapping contract in the module doc of
The urlPathPattern keeps the /orange-money-webpay/{env} prefix loose
on purpose: `dev` in the conformance suite and in compose.yml, but
country-specific in production, and a stub that hard-coded `dev`
would stop matching the moment someone tried the real prefix.
Commentary lives in `metadata` because WireMock fails to start on a
mapping document containing any field it does not recognise.
comment: The happy path, and the answer to every order_id no lower-numbered
priority claims -- including the server-generated references the
integration suite's confirms send. `pay_token` is templated from the
request's own `order_id` so a captured body says which call produced
which token, and so
redirect_confirm_commits_the_rails_material_before_it_answers can
assert the exact URL a random reference yields.
--global-response-templating is on
(vpay_testkit::containers::start_wiremock).
REF_DUPLICATE is NOT served from here: templating made the two
submits agree by construction, which is why it now has its own
scenario below.
201 with pay_token + payment_url + notif_token, per
docs/flows/adapter-orange-money.md.
The notif_url bodyPattern is a CONTRACT, added in Step 8 lane C, and the
twin of the X-Callback-Url matcher on MTN's requesttopay.json catch-all --
see that mapping's `why` for the whole argument. Orange's notification is
the only thing that can tell vpay a hosted-page payment finished before the
poll ladder's next rung, and a submit that carried no notif_url would be a
redirect rail settled by polling alone with nothing saying so.
The value is matched and not merely required to exist, because the PATH is
the half that drifts: vpay_api mounts POST /provider/{code}/callback and
vpay_config::ProviderHost::effective_callback_url derives it from
public_base_url, in two crates that do not compile against each other. The
host stays free (.+).
Decisive: change WebPaymentRequest's notif_url to config.base_url (or drop
the field) and this mapping stops matching -- WireMock answers 404 and the
adapter raises ProviderError::Config, failing
submit_returns_a_reference_and_a_flow_shaped_result and every Orange confirm
in backends/tests/integration.
The return_url/cancel_url bodyPatterns are a CONTRACT, added in Step 9 lane 2
alongside vpay_provider::ChargeRef::return_url (plan D2). A redirect rail that
was not told where the payer goes next strands them on the rail's own page, and
before D2 this adapter answered that per-charge question out of DEPLOYMENT
settings -- so every payer on a deployment came back to the same place whatever
the merchant had asked for, and nothing anywhere said so.
The matcher is `^https?://.+` and NOT an equality, nor a prefix under the
deployment's public_base_url, deliberately: the value is by design sometimes
vpay's own return page (a session-driven charge) and sometimes the MERCHANT's URL
on their own site (a direct /v1 or /v1/browser confirm, which is what closes
browser-checkout's D4). A mapping demanding vpay's own origin would refuse exactly
the second case. The EXACT value is asserted instead by the conformance case
the_submit_tells_the_rail_where_to_send_the_payer_back, over the request journal,
and end to end by confirm_rails.rs.
Decisive: drop `return_url` from vpay_adapter_orange_money's WebPaymentRequest and
this mapping stops matching -- WireMock answers 404, the adapter raises
ProviderError::Config, and both that conformance case and every Orange confirm in
backends/tests/integration fail. Measured, 2026-09-04.
payment_url now carries the two URLs it was given as query parameters, which is
what lets stub-hosted-page.json render links to them. See that file for why a stub
may do this and the real Orange page does not.
REF_DUPLICATE gets its own pair of mappings, as a WireMock SCENARIO, so that
duplicate_submit_reports_submitted_not_an_error can be decisive on this rail.
Under the priority-5 catch-all alone the Orange half of that case was the
accepted case run twice: the catch-all templates pay_token from the request's
own order_id, so the two submits could not have disagreed however the adapter
behaved, and the assertion `both are Ok` held for a rail that had never been
asked the question. This scenario CAN answer differently on the second call --
the state advances from Started to `resubmitted` and a separate mapping serves
it -- and it deliberately answers the SAME pay_token, which is the mechanism
Orange documents: a repeated order_id re-issues the token already minted for
it (docs/flows/adapter-orange-money.md).
Decisiveness was checked by hand: change the `resubmitted` mapping's pay_token
to pay-dup-2 and the conformance case fails on the pay_token equality
assertion. Restore it afterwards.
The return_url/cancel_url matchers are the same contract the catch-all carries,
repeated here so a duplicate submit cannot be the one call that quietly stops
telling the rail where the payer goes.

mappings.name: webpayment: REF_DUPLICATE, second submit — the SAME pay-dup-1

comment: The second and every later submit of the same order_id. Each conformance case
starts its own container, so the scenario always begins in `Started` -- the
same property requesttopay-scenario.json relies on.
The return_url/cancel_url matchers are the same contract the catch-all carries,
repeated here so a duplicate submit cannot be the one call that quietly stops
telling the rail where the payer goes.
A refused submit. Design §4 asked for this on the literal order_id
`bad-order`; that value is unreachable from the adapter, which always
sends `reference_id.to_string()` — so the reference here is a UUID,
chosen to mirror the MTN mappings' `…0400`. No conformance case uses
it yet: it exists so `submit`'s 4xx branch has something to be
pointed at by hand, and so a future case has a stub to bind to.
Orange documents no error-code vocabulary for this call, so the
adapter maps it to Rejected{provider_error} carrying the raw body —
'unmapped, carries the raw reason' (docs/flows/failures.md), which is
a thing to alert on rather than a settled mapping.

mappings.name: 307 whose Location must never be requested

comment: REF_REDIRECT, and the reason it is a 307 rather than a 302: a 307 replays the
request BODY, and this rail's submit body carries merchant_key. reqwest's default
policy would have followed it, so vpay_provider::http builds every client with
redirect::Policy::none() and the adapter must see the 307 itself.
The Location is a path on THIS SAME stub deliberately -- a cross-host target would
pass for the wrong reason, because an unroutable host errors out whatever the
policy is. See the mapping below, which must stay unrequested.

mappings.name: the Location is never requested (an accepted submit if it ever is)

comment: The rail's ACCEPTED answer, so a followed redirect makes submit return
Ok(Submitted) and the conformance case's expect_err fails loudly before the
request-count assertion even runs. Two independent failures for one regression.
